messages:
maya: Heads-up — customer report: sudden p95 spike for /v1/realtime/generate in us-west. Started ~09:10 UTC. They see auth token refresh timeouts and intermittent 500s. Anyone oncall?
sre-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1744444444 — paging oncall.
arjun: I'm on it. Any graphs?
maya: https://grafana.redwood/realtime/usw2 — p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~1.1s at 09:10. p99 ~2.6s. CPU looks fine, NVMe write lat p95 spiked and device queue depth is high.
lia: We rolled kernel 5.15.87 + cuda-driver-525 to us-west last night and gpu-fw 1.2.4 landed yesterday.
dev-fw: Could be host kernel + fw interaction causing hostfs flush storms. kvcache eviction counts spiked in the same window.
arjun: Repro from customer: 50 concurrent realtime streams -> see auth proxy token refresh timeouts ~1.2s and occasional 502/500.
maya: Attaching logs they pasted: 
```
2026-03-17T09:12:05Z ERROR auth-proxy timeout=1209ms token_refresh
2026-03-17T09:12:06Z WARN nvme qdepth=1024 dev=/dev/nvme0n1 write_lat_p95=78ms write_lat_p99=1.3s
```
lia: Any sign autoscaler or sidecar backpressure?
arjun: Autoscaler didn't fire — aggregate traffic stayed within expected. Observed continuous-batching queue length grow and KV cache misses +4x.
dev-fw: Quick mitigation options: 1) route live traffic away from updated pool to legacy nodes, 2) enable aggressive kvcache pinning, 3) throttle token-refresh concurrency. Lia, can you change routing weights?
lia: Updating routing now — adding fallback to us-west-legacy by weight.
sre-bot: Routing change applied: traffic shift 40% -> us-west-legacy (by weight).
maya: Customer reported immediate improvement: p95 dropped to ~190ms, p99 ~600ms after shift. :thumbsup:
csm-ops: I'll tell the customer we're routing to legacy and request they run a repro. Sending them a test script link.
arjun: For root cause we need:
- host kernel + driver versions per node
- nvme firmware + queue-depth histograms
- kvcache hit/miss metrics
- auth-proxy timing + DB token refresh latency
dev-fw: Also run `nvidia-smi topo -g` and `dmesg | grep -i nvme` on impacted hosts.
lia: Dumping host metadata and logs now, uploading to incident doc.
maya: Next steps: 1) backfill telemetry 08:30-09:30 (arjun) 2) reproduce in staging with same kernel + gpu-fw (dev-fw + eng-runtime) 3) if repro confirmed, plan targeted rollback of kernel/driver in us-west (lia + infra) 4) customer RCA & postmortem (maya + csm-ops).
arjun: I'll run a bisect between driver-525 vs driver-520 and nvme-fw versions. ETA ~2h.
dev-fw: If rollback needed prefer targeted canary nodes first — avoid fleet-wide immediate rollback.
csm-ops: Customer on hold until follow-up. I'll update them every 30m.
ops-jen: Prep'ing a canary rollback playbook now, will post in incident doc.
maya: Adding labels: severity=high, escalated=true.
sre-bot: Ticket updated: INC-2026-1744444444 severity=high assignees=@arjun,@dev-fw
lia: FWIW there's a related kube image push this morning — investigating if container runtime IO patterns changed.
arjun: Will post bisect updates. For now routing + KV pinning remain in place. Last metric check (09:23) shows p95 stable at ~200ms.
maya: Thanks team. Closing the Slack thread for now — continuing updates in incident doc. Good triage.
